solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Monday's issue is said to be so attractive

definitions.text: Monday's issue is said to be so
definitions.meaning: the nursery rhyme begins 'Monday's child is ...', describing that child's good looks
pleasant to look at, with pretty features

explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' here means offspring, the child of the old rhyme 'Monday's child', which tells each weekday's baby its fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone with a lovely face, so it means good-looking.

clue.text: A donkey almost berserk

indicators.note: almost means the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a moke is a British slang word for a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a donkey has very nearly gone wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final E of the donkey word; 'moke' is old British slang, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Running wild in a frenzy is the sense shared by the idiom and the adjective berserk.

clue.text: Sell or tell

definitions.meaning: to sell goods to the public, as a shop does
to recount or relate a story again

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a shop's selling to customers and a verb for recounting a tale.

clue.text: Right-wing extremist is twisting facts around

indicators.note: around tells us the shuffled letters go round the word is
twisting signals that the letters of facts are wrenched into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A political extremist is accused of distorting the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisting' and 'around' are two separate signals: one scrambles, the other wraps the scramble around the little word.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of authoritarian far-right nationalism is the classic right-wing extremist.

clue.text: A Frenchman meets a hospital nurse from China, originally

parts.note: M is the abbreviation of Monsieur, a Frenchman's title
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: An introduction story: a man from France meets a Chinese nurse at a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: The word was used in colonial East Asia, including China, for a wet nurse or maidservant.

clue.text: Appear very interested, then, to change employment

indicators.note: to change asks us to alter the order of the letters of then

parts.note: employment means use, as in putting something to use

explanation.surface: Someone shows great keenness about switching jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges THEN as ENTH, followed by USE. 'Employment' looks like a job but means use.
explanation.definitionFit: To gush with eagerness is to show strong interest outwardly.

clue.text: Soften the blow?

parts.note: read literally, a boxer holding back the force of a strike; figuratively, being gentle in criticism

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to restrain one's force, literally in boxing or figuratively in criticism.

clue.text: Essential employees in the security business?

definitions.meaning: staff whose jobs society cannot do without, such as nurses
humorously, locksmiths who cut and make keys

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names vital staff, and literally could be people who work on keys for locks.

clue.text: Bait and line cast on river

indicators.note: on places the first letter before the river in an across entry

parts.note: the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: An angler's kit: bait and a line cast out over the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' only adds to the fishing picture; the Ure is a North Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial bait used by anglers to attract fish is exactly this.

clue.text: Rival to study before exam — an exemplary worker

indicators.note: before places the study word ahead of the exam word

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
an exam is a test
the ant is the proverbial hard worker

explanation.surface: A competitor must revise before an exam to be a model employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taking part in a competition is a rival to the others.

clue.text: Hard getting permit to worship

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to permit is to allow

explanation.surface: A believer finds it hard to get permission to worship.
explanation.definitionFit: To honour as holy or sacred is to revere and venerate, a sense close to worship.

clue.text: Needle without an eye?

parts.note: Cleopatra's Needle in London is a stone monument, a needle with no hole for thread

explanation.walkthrough: Cleopatra's Needle is an ancient Egyptian stone pillar on London's Embankment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tapering four-sided stone pillar such as Cleopatra's Needle has no sewing eye.

clue.text: Not up to par playing on the green — embarrassing!

definitions.text: Not up to par playing on the green
definitions.meaning: a golfer below form when putting is said to be off at putting

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means disconcerting or unpleasant; read as two words it is a golfer's poor putting.

clue.text: Official title of great merit?

definitions.meaning: a form of address for an ambassador or governor
playfully, a quality of outstanding worth

explanation.definitionFit: It is the honorific for ambassadors and also suggests supreme quality.

clue.text: Incomplete sauce boat

indicators.note: incomplete means the sauce's name is cut short, losing its last two letters

parts.note: ketchup is a tomato sauce

explanation.surface: A gravy boat that is only partly filled with sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incomplete' removes UP from KETCHUP. 'Sauce boat' suggests a gravy jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-masted sailing vessel is a type of boat.

clue.text: He enters office uninvited

parts.note: suggests a gatecrasher at work, but means one who seizes a throne or post wrongfully

explanation.definitionFit: One who seizes power or position without right takes office uninvited.

clue.text: He finds seats for us above the woman

indicators.note: above places the first piece on top of the second in a down entry

parts.note: taken as written
the woman is her

explanation.surface: An attendant shows a couple to seats above a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre or church attendant shows people to their places.

clue.text: It may be perfect

parts.note: suggests flawlessness but refers to grammar, where perfect is a verb form

explanation.definitionFit: Perfect, as in 'I have done', is a grammatical verb form of this kind.

clue.text: Withdrawing of 101 meeting points

indicators.note: withdrawing means the little word of is pulled back, read right to left

parts.note: in Roman numerals C is 100 and I is one

explanation.surface: A course numbered 101 on where things meet, being dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawing' turns OF to FO; 101 is CI in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Points where lines or rays converge are focal points, plural of focus.

clue.text: Small number backed Church in the old days

indicators.note: backed means the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: No. is the short form of number
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A few people supported the church in times gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses the abbreviation; 'Small number' looks like a quantity but is the short written form of the word number.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly or at one time is the adverbial sense here.

clue.text: Chase around pines

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of chase are moved about

explanation.surface: Someone runs about among pine trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pines' looks like trees but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine is to long or yearn, and to ache for something is the same.

clue.text: Bill and Cyril spilt paint, maybe?

parts.note: AC is short for account, which is a bill

indicators.note: spilt suggests the letters of the name tumble out in disorder

explanation.surface: Two decorators, Bill and Cyril, knock over a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilt' rearranges CYRIL as RYLIC. Bill looks like a man's name but is an account.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic resin paint is one kind, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Politician's chosen — a Tory, partly towards the right

indicators.note: partly says the answer is contained within the phrase, leaning rightward politically in surface

explanation.surface: A party member has been chosen, a Conservative leaning right.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit within 'chosen a Tory'.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a senate is a politician.

clue.text: Open at lunch breaks

indicators.note: breaks signals the letters of at lunch are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A shop opens during lunch breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' looks like a noun for rest periods but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To release a door's fastening is to open it.

clue.text: Stretches between bends

parts.note: reads like exercises between bending down, but means straight sections of river

explanation.definitionFit: Straight sections of a river between its curves are called this, and the verb also means stretches.

clue.text: Rice, for example, that's eaten for breakfast

definitions.meaning: rice is a kind of grain crop
a morning dish such as cornflakes

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a grain like rice and a breakfast food served with milk.

clue.text: Score is two-love

definitions.meaning: a 2-0 result read as figures gives 20

explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, and the digits two and nought (love) together make the same number.

clue.text: Repair that's right inside and wrong outside

definitions.text: Repair that's right inside and wrong outside

parts.words: Repair that's right inside and wrong outside
parts.note: ... stitches show on the right side of fabric and the wrong side, sounding moral

explanation.definitionFit: A mend of a hole in knitwear is made with woven stitches through both faces of the cloth.

clue.text: Permit that'll get you across a mountain

definitions.text: that'll get you across a mountain
definitions.meaning: a col or gap through a mountain range

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an entry permit and a route through mountains.

clue.text: Sort of lady we hate to precede

indicators.note: sort of signals that the letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes a type of woman they dislike going first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' looks like a vague hedge but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To go first and guide others is to precede them.

clue.text: Lift and cut

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to steal and a small cut or notch.

clue.text: Take to heart?

parts.note: suggests being affected emotionally but means move things to the middle

explanation.definitionFit: To bring control or activity to a central point is to move it to the heart of things.
